
The NVIDIA DGX Spark is designed to operate with an ideal ambient temperature range of ==**5°C to 30°C (41°F to 86°F)**==. ![NVIDIA Docs](data:image/jpeg;base64,)NVIDIA Docs

However, under heavy AI training or inference workloads, the internal components, specifically the GB10 GPU/CPU, can reach significantly higher temperatures. 

**Key Temperature Findings:**

- **Operating Temps:** The system often operates in the **50°C to 60°C** range during normal or slightly intensive processes.
- **Thermal Throttling & High Load:** Under intense workloads, temperatures frequently climb to **90°C–95°C**, causing noticeable token/sec performance drops due to thermal throttling.
- **Shutdown Threshold:** Many users report that the system triggers automatic shutdowns when temperatures reach around **95°C** (203°F) during prolonged high-load scenarios like Llama pretraining.
- **Optimal High-Load Cooling:** With additional cooling solutions (such as external fans or custom racks), users have successfully kept the max temperature lower, around **72°C**. ![NVIDIA Developer Forums](data:image/jpeg;base64,)NVIDIA Developer Forums +4

It is recommended to maintain adequate airflow around the unit to prevent it from reaching the critical shutdown threshold. ![NVIDIA Developer Forums](data:image/jpeg;base64,)NVIDIA Developer Forums

# [spark-gpu-throttle-check](https://github.com/hoesing/spark-gpu-throttle-check)
A diagnostic tool for detecting GPU clock throttling on NVIDIA DGX Spark (and related GB10) systems suspected to be caused by bad USB Power Delivery (PD) negotiation.
https://github.com/hoesing/spark-gpu-throttle-check
